sentences.text: The petitioner submits that he is a retail seller of Ice cream who took a room for rent in the year 2024 from the 4 th respondent.
Petitioner submits that he had obtained a licence from the Commissioner of Food Safety under the provisions of the FSSAI Act, 2006.

Petitioner conceded that despite receiving Ext.P5 notice from the Municipality on 06.08.2024, directing him to function only with a trade licence, he has not stopped the business or applied for a licence.
2. Upon admission of the writ petition, an interim order was granted by this Court on 03.09.2024 and the same is still in force.

Taking note of the fact that the petitioner has not made any application for a licence as directed in Ext.P5, there will be a direction to the petitioner to file an appropriate application for a trade licence before the Municipality within a week from today.

W.P.(C)
Nos.36684, 30827, 34172, 34613, 35660 of 2024 2024:KER:89781 Orders shall be passed on the same within three weeks thereafter with notice to the petitioner, in accordance with law.
Since this Court had granted an interim order as aforesaid, the status quo as of today shall be maintained for a period of one month.
The writ petition is disposed of as above.
The petitioners were served with Ext.P4 notice directing him to take a licence.

Admittedly, the petitioners are functioning without a trade licence from the Municipality.
2. Taking note of the fact that the petitioner has not made any application for a licence as directed in Ext.P4, there will be a direction to the petitioners to file an appropriate application for a trade licence before the Municipality within a week from today.
Orders shall be passed on the same within three weeks thereafter with notice to the petitioners, in accordance with law.
Since this Court passed an order on 03.09.2024, in the light of the licence granted by the FSSAI Authority, the interim order will continue for one more month.
The writ petition is disposed of as above.

W.P.(C) Nos.36684, 30827, 34172, 34613, 35660 of 2024 2024:KER:89781 W.P.(C) No.34172 of 2024 is filed by the Varkala Municipality seeking an expeditious disposal of Ext.P3 Appeal, Appeal No.609 of 2018 preferred by the 4th respondent in W.P.(C) 34613 of 2024.
The same person had filed Appeal No.136 of 2024 before the Tribunal.
The Municipality seeks an expeditious disposal of both the above cases.
Both appeals were preferred against orders passed under Section 406(3) of the Kerala Municipality Act, alleging unauthorised constructions.
The Municipality submits that in view of the pendency of these appeals and the interim stay granted, they are unable to take any action against those constructions which were totally unauthorised.

Taking note of the fact that Ext.P3 appeal was filed in the year 2018 and that Appeal No.136 of 2024 was also filed by the same person, there will be a direction to the Tribunal for Local Self Government Institutions, Thiruvananthapuram to take the appeal and pass orders, in accordance with law, after hearing the parties, within two months from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioner submits that he is a retail seller of Ice cream who took a room for rent in the year 2024 from the 4 th respondent.
Petitioner submits that he had obtained a licence from the Commissioner of Food Safety under the provisions of the FSSAI Act, 2006.
Petitioner conceded that despite receiving Ext.P5 notice from the Municipality on 06.08.2024, directing him to function only with a trade licence, he has not stopped the business or applied for a licence.
2. Upon admission of the writ petition, an interim order was granted by this Court on 03.09.2024 and the same is still in force.
The petitioners were served with Ext.P4 notice directing him to take a licence.
Admittedly, the petitioners are functioning without a trade licence from the Municipality.
2. Taking note of the fact that the petitioner has not made any application for a licence as directed in Ext.P4, there will be a direction to the petitioners to file an appropriate application for a trade licence before the Municipality within a week from today.
The same person had filed Appeal No.136 of 2024 before the Tribunal.
Both appeals were preferred against orders passed under Section 406(3) of the Kerala Municipality Act, alleging unauthorised constructions.
2. The Municipality had filed a counter, stating that proceedings were taken against the owner of the building alleging unauthorised constructions and they are pending before the Tribunal for Local Self Government Institutions.
The petitioner was issued with Ext.P5 notice directing him to take a licence.
